svg.text: near-field — error(B) against the fully-refined tree
t_max = 20, n_sync = 49, N = 8, E+1 = 8, eta = 0.01, levels = 7, 1024x1024, f64, criterion = display colouring
error = 0 means MATCHES THIS SAMPLING, not correct: the reference is the fully-refined tree at one sample per pixel, and at the screen floor sub-pixel structure is sampled arbitrarily.
greedy_oracle is a strong reference, NOT a ceiling. A criterion beating it indicates lookahead value, not a bug: on a tree, gains are neither independent nor immediately available.

A label reading (k/n) means n-k points were non-finite and were DROPPED. A high NaN fraction is a property to read, not a defect: term_grad is NaN on 97.1% of near-field and still reaches zero by B = 383.
